sections.body:
```python name=architecture/clean_architecture.py
# ============================================================
# CLEAN ARCHITECTURE / LAYERED ARCHITECTURE
# ============================================================
"""
Layer Structure (from outside to inside):

┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PRESENTATION LAYER (Routers/API)       │ ← FastAPI endpoints
│    Handles HTTP request/response        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  SERVICE LAYER (Business Logic)         │ ← Pure Python logic
│    Orchestrates use cases               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  REPOSITORY LAYER (Data Access)         │ ← SQLAlchemy queries
│    Abstracts database operations        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  DOMAIN LAYER (Entities/Models)         │ ← Pydantic + SQLAlchemy models
│    Core business objects                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

RULES:
- Inner layers NEVER depend on outer layers
- Dependencies point INWARD
- Business logic is in Services, NOT in routers
- Routers are thin — they just call services
- Repositories are the ONLY layer that talks to the database
"""

# --- Domain (Schemas) ---
from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr

class UserCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: EmailStr

class UserResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str

# --- Repository (Data Access) ---
from typing import Protocol

class UserRepositoryProtocol(Protocol):
    async def create(self, user_data: dict) -> dict: ...
    async def get_by_id(self, user_id: int) -> dict | None: ...
    async def get_by_email(self, email: str) -> dict | None: ...
    async def list_all(self, skip: int, limit: int) -> list[dict]: ...

class SQLAlchemyUserRepository:
    def __init__(self, session):
        self.session = session
    
    async def create(self, user_data: dict) -> dict:
        # SQLAlchemy logic here
        pass
    
    async def get_by_id(self, user_id: int) -> dict | None:
        pass
    
    async def get_by_email(self, email: str) -> dict | None:
        pass
    
    async def list_all(self, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
        pass

# --- Service (Business Logic) ---
class UserService:
    def __init__(self, repo: UserRepositoryProtocol):
        self.repo = repo
    
    async def create_user(self, data: UserCreate) -> UserResponse:
        # Business rules
        existing = await self.repo.get_by_email(data.email)
        if existing:
            raise ValueError(f"Email {data.email} already registered")
        
        user = await self.repo.create(data.model_dump())
        return UserResponse(**user)
    
    async def get_user(self, user_id: int) -> UserResponse:
        user = await self.repo.get_by_id(user_id)
        if not user:
            raise ValueError(f"User {user_id} not found")
        return UserResponse(**user)

# --- Router (Presentation) ---
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException

router = APIRouter(prefix="/users", tags=["Users"])

async def get_user_service() -> UserService:
    # Dependency injection
    # In real app: get DB session, create repo, create service
    pass

@router.post("/", response_model=UserResponse, status_code=201)
async def create_user(
    data: UserCreate,
    service: UserService = Depends(get_user_service),
):
    try:
        return await service.create_user(data)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=str(e))
```
